harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3, each on its own subnet: node1 eth1=172.20.10.1/24 (toward node2), eth2=172.20.20.1/24 (toward node3), with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. node2 eth1=172.20.10.2/24 with a static route to 172.20.20.0/24 via node1; node3 eth1=172.20.20.2/24 with a static route to 172.20.10.0/24 via node1. Verified node2<->node3 reachability across the VLAN boundary. Persisted config so it survives reboot: node1 via a new systemd oneshot unit ([REDACTED].service, enabled) that reapplies eth1/eth2 addressing and forwarding sysctls (and strips docker0's class-E leftover address) at boot; node2/node3 via NetworkManager connection profiles (nmcli con mod eth1 ipv4.method manual ...) with autoconnect enabled. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured each node's boot_id baseline and a healthy routing/connectivity proof, issued a native reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a changed boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified interface config, routes, and end-to-end ping recovered post-restart. One gap found and fixed during node2's restart: its eth1 NetworkManager profile had autoconnect=no, so the static IP/route did not come back automatically after reboot; fixed by setting connection.autoconnect=yes on node2 (and proactively on node3 before its restart), after which node3's subsequent restart auto-recovered without manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected topology and interfaces on node1 (SONiC-VS/Debian, eth0 mgmt + eth1/eth2 dataplane) and node2/node3 (RHEL7, eth0 mgmt + eth1 dataplane)
Neutralized node1 docker0 class-E leftover address per SONiC guidance
Assigned node1 eth1=172.20.10.1/24, eth2=172.20.20.1/24; enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding
Assigned node2 eth1=172.20.10.2/24 with route to 172.20.20.0/24 via 172.20.10.1; assigned node3 eth1=172.20.20.2/24 with route to 172.20.10.0/24 via 172.20.20.1
Verified bidirectional ping between node2 and node3 across node1
Persisted node1 config via new systemd unit [REDACTED].service (enabled, runs at boot)
Persisted node2/node3 config via nmcli con mod on existing eth1 NetworkManager profiles (static IPv4 + static route + never-default)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline for all three nodes

Restarted node1 via `reboot` (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1/eth2 config and forwarding sysctls restored by the systemd unit, verified ping recovery

Restarted node2, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, found eth1 profile had autoconnect=no (IP/route missing post-reboot), fixed by enabling autoconnect and bringing connection up, verified ping recovery
Proactively set node3 eth1 autoconnect=yes before its restart
Restarted node3, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id, verified eth1 static IP/route came back automatically via NetworkManager, verified bidirectional ping recovery

evidence.summary: eth1=172.20.10.1/24, eth2=172.20.20.1/24 assigned; ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls set to 1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 addressed in their own VLAN subnets with routes to the peer subnet via node1
node2 and node3 reach each other across the VLAN boundary (initial proof)
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping success 172.20.10.2<->172.20.20.2 through node1 before any restart

evidence.requirement: persistence of node1 routing config across reboot
evidence.summary: systemd oneshot unit [REDACTED].service created, enabled, and active, reapplying eth1/eth2 addressing and forwarding at boot

evidence.requirement: persistence of node2/node3 routing config across reboot
evidence.summary: NetworkManager eth1 profiles set to static IPv4 with static routes to peer subnet, activated

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=ce04f497-f2df-464f-9395-7af97e208809; eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls confirmed healthy

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: reboot acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=3d2cac9a-ef44-4fbf-8e28-0f6eb48d34fa, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: recovered state and connectivity
evidence.summary: [REDACTED].service active post-boot with eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding restored; ping recovers between node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id=73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31 confirmed twice; ping to node3 succeeded pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: reboot acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: sudo-backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=74d3be55-3e2a-4db2-ac0c-7ba4423d3f3f, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: recovered state and connectivity (with fix)
evidence.summary: Post-boot eth1/route missing (autoconnect=no); NM profile config confirmed intact; fixed autoconnect and brought connection up; ping to node3 recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Proactively set autoconnect=yes on node3 eth1; boot_id=d7a80301-53d3-4cc8-bd41-1293f67d0769 confirmed baseline

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: reboot acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: sudo-backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id=0ffca916-dd41-4da2-8610-2ee1eba5f1d5, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: recovered state and connectivity
evidence.summary: eth1 auto-reconnected with static IP/route intact post-boot without manual intervention; ping succeeded both directions (node3->node2 and node2->node3)
